question: How do the saved stablecoin-law cards compare issuance, backing and redemption?
answer: The saved July 28 cards compare who may issue, backing, custody/distribution, redemption or settlement and legal limits. Each keeps its own legal object and historical status; the comparison is not a current legal survey.

groups.note: cat values are the page's four categories (see chapter.cats): active = law in force, enacted = enacted but not yet in force, watch = under discussion, adjacent = related payment or market law.

items.title: European Union: stablecoins need a license as e-money or asset-backed tokens
kv: The stablecoin parts of MiCA, the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation, apply from 30 Jun 2024. The rest of MiCA applies from 30 Dec 2024.
Only a credit institution or an electronic-money institution may issue an e-money token. Issuers of asset-referenced tokens need a separate authorization.
Duties on reserves, liquidity, keeping assets separate, custody and redemption at any time differ by token type. E-money token holders can redeem at face value. Paying interest on them is prohibited.
Who may sell or hold it for you
Crypto-asset service providers need an EU-wide authorization and follow EU-wide conduct rules.
The token may move on a blockchain. Issuer redemption and bank or central-bank money settle separately, each final at its own time.
A strong legal base for connecting services. We do not claim contactless card software (EMV) reads MiCA tokens directly.
The euro system favors one equal-value euro (monetary singleness) and regulated private claims over an unlimited token market.
Europe regulates by legal type of token. It is the clearest category-first model.
MiCA authorization is not a European Central Bank (ECB) guarantee, deposit insurance, or acceptance by every merchant.

items.title: United Arab Emirates: stores may accept only licensed dirham tokens
kv: The Payment Token Services Regulation of the Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE) has been in force since 31 Aug 2024.

A UAE company may be licensed to issue a Dirham Payment Token; a bank issues through a subsidiary or affiliate. Issuing, converting, holding and transferring foreign tokens each need their own permission.

By default, reserves are 100% cash in the same currency, held in a separate escrow account at an unrelated UAE bank. A qualifying bank-owned issuer may hold at least 50% cash and the rest in short UAE government or CBUAE instruments, with extra capital and controls.
Who may sell or hold it for you
Issuing, holding and transferring, and converting tokens are separate regulated services.
The wallet transfer is the customer's part. Reserve cash and redemption are separate parts, at a commercial bank or, when directed, in central-bank custody.
This is the clearest comparison for paying in stores. An ordinary UAE merchant may accept only a licensed Dirham Payment Token. Registered foreign tokens may be used only to buy virtual assets.
The law protects the dirham's role in payments by controlling which legal tokens merchants may accept, not by controlling the contactless hardware.
The UAE shows that legal routing and merchant permission decide stablecoin acceptance, not contactless (NFC) capability.
A terminal that supports contactless payment does not meet the rules on token licensing, conversion, custody, merchants or redemption.

items.title: United States: the GENIUS Act sets who may issue and what they must hold
kv: Public Law 119-27 was signed 18 Jul 2025. Final implementing rules were due 18 Jul 2026. We found none on official final-rule pages through the 28 Jul cutoff. The latest general effective date is still 18 Jan 2027. It moves earlier only if final rules start the 120-day countdown.
Permitted issuers are subsidiaries of insured depository institutions, federal qualified issuers, or state qualified issuers, divided by the law's federal–state split and size threshold.

Reserves must match coins one-to-one: cash, central-bank balances, insured deposits, Treasury bills of 93 days or less, qualifying repurchase agreements (repo), government money funds and related liquid government assets. Issuers report monthly. Holders get no interest and no FDIC insurance.
Who may sell or hold it for you
Wallets, card networks, processors and distributors can be separate companies from the legal issuer. A restriction on service providers starts in 2028, setting a later deadline for market access.
Blockchain transfer, card-network obligation, minting and redemption, bank-deposit movement and central-bank final settlement stay separate.
GENIUS supplies the lawful issuer and reserves that a card, wallet or merchant processor (acquirer) can route. It does not update any terminal.
The reserve rules directly create demand for short-term Treasury bills. The dollar stays the unit, and private companies still distribute the coins.
enacted · not yet generally in effect
Of these laws, GENIUS most directly links more stablecoins to more government-debt purchases for reserves. It also shows most clearly that stablecoin law is banking law too.
Enacted does not mean in effect. A proposal, a charter application or a conditional approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) is not a live GENIUS issuer authorization.

items.title: Hong Kong: issuing a stablecoin requires a license from the Hong Kong Monetary Authority
kv: The Stablecoins Ordinance and the supervisory framework of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) took effect 1 Aug 2025.
Issuing an in-scope stablecoin tied to a government currency (fiat-referenced) in Hong Kong requires a license. So do specified issuing or offering activities linked to Hong Kong.
HKMA supervision focuses on reserve management, redemption, risk management, governance, anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing (AML/CFT) controls, and disclosure.
Who may sell or hold it for you
Only specified regulated institutions may offer in-scope stablecoins to retail investors. The issuer's license and the permission to distribute are separate.
The Ordinance covers the issuer and the token's promise, not the merchant's card processor (acquirer) or the final bank-money payment.
A licensed stablecoin can fund or settle payments behind an existing wallet or card. The legal link still needs an authorized distributor and processor.
Hong Kong protects its monetary system by licensing issuers and supervising them locally. It does not treat every token as bank money.
Hong Kong uses licensing by the regulator: a strict issuer license in an international financial center.
A sandbox place, a license application or a public announcement is not a license.

items.title: United Kingdom: issuing stablecoins becomes a licensed activity; the full regime is expected to start in late 2027
kv: The 2026 cryptoasset regulations make issuing and safeguarding regulated activities. The wider regime is expected to begin in late 2027. The Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) still has to make rules and set application steps.
Issuing a UK qualifying stablecoin becomes a regulated activity. For systemic payment stablecoins, the Bank of England adds oversight to FCA supervision.
Qualifying stablecoins are tied to a government currency and hold backing assets. Detailed FCA rules are expected to provide full backing and redemption rights.
Who may sell or hold it for you
Safeguarding and other crypto activities need separate permissions. The government is still settling what the dealing and payment-services rules cover.
The UK is explicitly designing stablecoins as both cryptoassets and possible payment instruments, with separate oversight of systemic ones.
Promising law for connecting services, but the payment-services rules are not finished.
The UK goes in order: what the law covers first, payments integration second, tax treatment third.
Britain is the best example of a license requirement already in law whose operating rules are still being written.
Do not call the late-2027 regime live. Current policy notes explicitly describe more rules and payments reform still to come.

items.title: South Korea: a bank-led won stablecoin is under discussion, not law
kv: The Digital Asset Committee of Korea's Financial Services Commission (FSC) discussed the government review draft. Legislation and the final design for issuers are not settled.
A bank-centered model, including a debated consortium with banks holding 50%+1, was discussed, not adopted.
Who may sell or hold it for you
Not final. Existing bank-token and wholesale-settlement pilots are separate from any won-stablecoin law.
The Bank of Korea's work puts central-bank and commercial-bank money first, with stablecoins as a supplementary option.
Korea runs advanced payment and token pilots, but they have not led to an enacted law for paying merchants directly in stablecoins.
What institutions are actually working on is tokenizing bank deposits and testing wholesale settlement. The rules for stablecoin issuers remain open.
Korea is the comparison case: strong technical readiness does not mean settled law.
A committee discussion or a bank proof of concept is not a won-stablecoin law.

items.title: Japan: trust-issued stablecoins may hold up to half their reserves in short government bonds
kv: Japan's 2022 rules for electronic payment instruments (EPIs) have applied since 1 Jun 2023. The main parts of Act No. 66 of 2025 and its final implementing rules took effect 1 Jun 2026.
Banks, registered funds-transfer providers, and trust companies or trust banks issue different legal claims. A lighter intermediary that holds no customer assets may broker for a full provider.

Covered trust stablecoins may hold up to 50% in qualifying government bonds of three months or less, or in term deposits that can be withdrawn early without losing principal. At least 50% stays in demand deposits. Rules on daily fair-value measurement and fixing shortfalls apply.
Who may sell or hold it for you
Full EPI providers handle sale, exchange, brokering or custody. The lighter intermediary cannot hold customer assets.
Trust redemption, deposit-token settlement, bank reserves and a public-blockchain transfer are different things. Each settles on its own timeline.
Japan is setting the legal roles for issuers, intermediaries and redemption. A payment service provider could keep the tap while changing funding or payout behind it.

Yen Currency Watch grades for stability and payment use: underlying order B; exchange order B; current-payment usability A; systemic service A. The yen is absorbing the change in an orderly way, not showing a broken payment system.
Like GENIUS, Japan lets reserves fund government debt, but more narrowly: only trust stablecoins may hold limited short government bonds.
JPYSC running on controlled venues is not open-wallet circulation at merchants. Tokenized bank deposits are not trust stablecoins.

items.title: Japan: crypto trading moves under securities law; stablecoins stay under payments law
kv: The Diet (Japan's parliament) passed the Financial Instruments and Exchange Act (FIEA) and Payment Services Act (PSA) reform 15 Jul 2026. Its main parts start on a Cabinet-set date within the legal window.
This is not a new stablecoin issuer category. Stablecoins, as electronic payment instruments, stay under the PSA.
This card covers no change to stablecoin reserves.
Who may sell or hold it for you
Rules on trading, offerings, lending, management, advice, disclosure, intermediary duties and unfair trading move under the FIEA.
The law deliberately keeps market regulation separate from the settlement of payment money.
The law helps institutions classify crypto investment activity. It does not make crypto a means of contactless payment.
Japan is building two legal paths: payments law for money claims that can be redeemed, and market law for cryptoassets held as investments.
The split is the key point. Japan keeps ‘crypto,’ ‘stablecoin’ and ‘bank deposit’ as separate legal things.
Do not say Japan made every cryptoasset a security, legal tender or a bank deposit.

items.title: Japan: paper checks and bills to stop clearing from April 2027 (a plan, not a stablecoin law)
kv: The plan aims for zero paper bills and checks through the electronic clearinghouse by the end of FY2026, and an end to paper exchange from the start of FY2027.
Banks still owe the payment; only the form of the payment instruction changes.
Who may sell or hold it for you
Electronically recorded monetary claims and internet transfers replace presenting paper.
This is a direct move from cash and checks to electronic payment systems, separate from stablecoin law.
It is the closest historical parallel in this set: the paper instrument disappears while the bank relationship stays.
A mature currency system can retire an old payment instrument without changing the unit of account.
official transition plan from industry and government
Japan is changing both ends at once. It is retiring paper claims while making new tokenized claims legal.
This is an official transition plan. It is not a stablecoin law, and it does not prove every check disappears on one day.

catalog_context.title: Crypto around the world: many licenses, no proven cross-border use
catalog_context.answer: Across 22 jurisdictions, we found no verified cross-border payment route that depends on crypto from end to end. The token layer still settles through ordinary banks and national payment systems.
